name: upgrade-dev-20
purpose: Development set for Refit's upgrade benchmark: 20 public JavaScript/TypeScript and Python repos (12 npm, 8 PyPI), each pinned at a default-branch commit where it still runs on an end-of-life Node.js or Python (12 repos) or an old framework major (8 repos: Vue 2, Nuxt 2, Next.js 12 and 14, React 16, Express 4, Django 3.2, Flask 2.2), with a real test suite. Each entry lists every line that declares the old version, so a run can check that the upgrade moved all of them and that the tests still pass.
criteria: Curated by hand on 2026-11-06, not recovered from Refit's history. Status read that day: endoflife.date (api/nodejs.json, api/python.json) gives Node 14 EOL 2023-04-30, 16 2023-09-11, 18 2025-04-30, 20 2026-04-30 (supported: 22, 24, 26) and Python 3.6 EOL 2021-12-23, 3.7 2023-06-27, 3.8 2024-10-07, 3.9 2025-10-31; nodejs.org/en/about/previous-releases lists Node 14, 16, 18 and 20 as EOL, and devguide.python.org/versions lists the same Python dates; Python 3.10 also reached end of life on 2026-10-01 per the devguide, but this set's cutoff is Node <= 20 and Python <= 3.9, so 3.10 lines are not recorded in declaredIn. Framework status from the frameworks' own pages: Vue 2 EOL 2023-12-31, Nuxt 2 EOL 2024-06-30, Next.js 12-14 listed as unsupported (16 is Active LTS), React 19 stable 2024-12-05, Express 5 announced 2024-10-15, Django 3.2 out of support since 2024-04-01, Flask 3.0.0 released 2023-09-30. Candidates came from GitHub repository search (`language:JavaScript stars:30..3000 pushed:>2025-10-15 size:<30000 archived:false fork:false`, `language:TypeScript stars:30..3000 pushed:>2025-10-15 size:<30000 archived:false fork:false`, `language:Python stars:30..3000 pushed:>2025-10-15 size:<30000 archived:false fork:false`, `language:TypeScript stars:20..2000 pushed:>2025-11-01 size:<30000 archived:false fork:false`, `topic:nextjs stars:10..3000 pushed:>2025-10-15 size:<40000 archived:false fork:false`, `topic:vue stars:10..3000 pushed:>2025-10-15 size:<40000 archived:false fork:false`, `topic:django stars:10..3000 pushed:>2025-10-15 size:<40000 archived:false fork:false`, `topic:react stars:20..3000 pushed:>2025-10-01 size:<30000 archived:false fork:false`, `topic:expressjs stars:20..3000 pushed:>2025-10-01 size:<30000 archived:false fork:false`, and first passes `topic:nextjs stars:20..3000 pushed:2023-01-01..2025-09-01 size:<50000 archived:false fork:false`, `topic:vue stars:20..3000 pushed:2022-12-01..2025-10-01 size:<50000 archived:false fork:false`, `topic:nuxt stars:10..3000 pushed:2022-12-01..2025-10-01 size:<50000 archived:false fork:false`, `language:TypeScript stars:30..1500 pushed:2023-03-01..2025-08-01 size:<20000 archived:false fork:false`, `language:JavaScript stars:40..2000 pushed:2023-01-01..2025-06-30 size:<30000 archived:false fork:false`) and GitHub code search (`"node-version: 14" test path:.github/workflows` and the same for 14.x, 16, 16.x and 18, `node-version 14 "npm test" path:.github/workflows` and the same with 16, 18 and 20, `FROM node:20 filename:Dockerfile`, `"python-version: 3.6" pytest path:.github/workflows` and the same for 3.7, 3.8 and 3.9, `"manage.py test" path:.github/workflows`, `"manage.py test" "python-version: 3.8" path:.github/workflows` and the same with 3.6, 3.7 and 3.9, `FROM python:3.9 pytest filename:Dockerfile`, `"python-version: 3.8" "pip install -r requirements.txt" pytest path:.github/workflows`, `nuxt 2.15.8 jest filename:package.json`, `express supertest jest filename:package.json`, `flask pytest path:.github/workflows`, `Django==3.2 filename:requirements.txt`, `Django==4.1 filename:requirements.txt`, `Flask==1.1 filename:requirements.txt`, `Flask==1.1.4 filename:requirements.txt`, `Flask==2.0 filename:requirements.txt`, `Flask==2.0.3 filename:requirements.txt`, `Flask==2.2 pytest filename:requirements.txt`, `Flask==2.3 pytest filename:requirements.txt`). Most hits were too old: for many repos whose HEAD dates from 2023-2024 GitHub no longer lists any Actions run (and no check runs) on that commit, so there was nothing to cite, and the searches that worked were the ones limited to recent pushes. Each hit was screened by reading package.json, .nvmrc, .node-version, setup.py, pyproject.toml, tox.ini, requirements and Dockerfiles at the default-branch HEAD. Kept: public, not archived, not a fork or template, under 50 MB, pushed since 2022-11-06, a handful of stars or owned by a real organization, not owned by refit-dev and not in any other file under evals/sets/dev/; a test command plus test files; and, for 19 of 20, a GitHub Actions run on exactly the pinned commit whose workflow runs the tests and concluded success (ciRun). swellstores/origin-theme has no CI (evidence no-ci). Dropped: no Actions run left at HEAD (sapegin/mrm, nytimes/react-tracking) or tests workflow switched off (nemanjam/nextjs-prisma-boilerplate); CircleCI-only repos (AlisProject/frontend-application, nishinoshake/aws-rough, acmucsd/membership-portal); no test files (PostHog/HouseWatch, most Next.js and Nuxt starters); failing or cancelled CI (CityOfPhiladelphia/ais, signorrayan/RedTeam_toolkit, lobehub/lobe-vidol); native addons or heavy ML installs (Blizzard/node-rdkafka, ranisalt/node-argon2, benedekrozemberczki/pytorch_geometric_temporal); a 5-star teaching repo (sp41mer/drf-test-examples); san650/ember-cli-page-object (Node 14, but its tests need a browser); and, to keep the language and version mix, tediousjs/node-mssql, broofa/mime, cerebroapp/cerebro, apache/casbin-express-authz, kawalcovid19/wargabantuwarga.com, vxgmichel/aioconsole, wee-slack/wee-slack and HumeAI/hume-python-sdk. fromVersion is the runtime a repo runs on (Docker image, .nvmrc, its single CI version) or, for a library, its declared floor; toVersion is Node 24, Python 3.12 or the framework's current major (for Django the current LTS, 5.2, rather than 6.1). declaredIn holds every line at the pinned commit that sets or implies the EOL runtime (Node <= 20, Python <= 3.9) or the old framework major, including companion packages tied to it (vue-template-compiler, enzyme-adapter-react-16, Werkzeug 2); lockfiles, docs and comments are not recorded. Every declaredIn line was read at the pinned commit (re-check with `node evals/sets/check-callsites.ts upgrade-dev-20`), every quote was re-read on its page on 2026-11-06, and no repo code was installed or run. Repos are ordered by SHA-256 of "upgrade-dev-20:<owner/name>" (lower-cased), so a run with a small cap reaches them in an order nobody picked.

pendingChange.title: Vue 2 is past end of life

source.quote: Vue 2 will reach End of Life (EOL) on December 31st, 2023.

repos.why: A civic-tech app on Vue 2.7 + Vuetify 2 + Vue CLI with Vue 2-only test tooling (@vue/vue2-jest, @testing-library/vue 5); moving to Vue 3 drags Vuetify 3 and the test stack with it. It also pins Node 16 in .nvmrc and CI.

pendingChange.title: Python 3.8 is past end of life

source.quote: As of 2024-10-07, 3.8 has reached the end-of-life phase of its release cycle.

repos.why: A popular SVG charting library with python_requires >=3.8 and py38/py39 in tox and the CI matrix; a typical library floor bump across setup.py, tox and CI.

pendingChange.title: Python 3.7 is past end of life

source.quote: As of 2023-06-27, 3.7 has reached the end-of-life phase of its release cycle.

repos.why: A Django/PostgreSQL library whose floor is Python 3.7, with python_version-conditional test pins for 3.7-3.9, tox envs and a CI matrix to prune together; tests need a Postgres server (CI uses a service container).

pendingChange.title: Node.js 20 is past end of life

repos.why: An active React app whose only Node pin is .nvmrc 20.9.0, which every workflow reads through node-version-file; the upgrade is one line plus whatever the ejected CRA toolchain needs on Node 24.

pendingChange.title: Next.js 12 is unsupported; Next.js 16 is the current major

source.quote: Each major version will remain in Maintenance LTS for two years following the initial release.

repos.why: A library for Next.js getServerSideProps that develops and tests against Next 12 and React 17 (unit tests plus jest-playwright e2e pages); the upgrade has to move the dev pin, the peer range and the React 17 test stack.

pendingChange.title: Node.js 14 is past end of life

source.quote: Node.js 18 and all earlier versions are End-Of-Life.

repos.why: A small CLI library: engines and CI pin Node 14 and the publish job still runs Node 10, so the upgrade has to move all three while keeping the ava suite green.

pendingChange.title: Node.js 16 is past end of life

source.quote: We are moving the End-of-Life date of Node.js 16 by seven months to coincide with the end of support of OpenSSL 1.1.1 on September 11th, 2023.

repos.why: A popular browser extension that caps engines at <= 16.20.2 and pins Node 16.20.2 in .nvmrc and both workflows; lifting the cap on a webpack 4 / React 16 build is a realistic, non-trivial runtime upgrade.

pendingChange.title: Python 3.6 is past end of life

source.quote: As of 2021-12-23, 3.6 has reached the end-of-life phase of its release cycle.

repos.why: A pure-Python C++ header parser that still declares requires-python >=3.6 (with a dataclasses backport marker and black py36 target), builds on 3.8 and tests 3.7-3.13 in CI; a clean library floor bump with a large pytest suite.

pendingChange.title: Next.js 14 is unsupported; Next.js 16 is the current major

source.quote: Each major version will remain in Maintenance LTS for two years following the initial release.

repos.why: A pages-router app pinned to Next 14.2.35 with next-pwa and next-i18next; a common two-major Next upgrade checked by typecheck, vitest and next build. Its Dockerfile also pins node:18-alpine.

pendingChange.title: Django 3.2 is past end of life

source.quote: These release series no longer receive security updates or bug fixes.

tests.command: cd anytask && python manage.py compilemessages && python manage.py test

repos.why: A course and assignment tracking app (courses, schools, contests, issues) pinned to Django 3.2.25 with old django-* add-ons, running on Python 3.8 in Docker and CI; a real app-level Django upgrade checked by 20 test modules (CI starts a MinIO service for S3).

pendingChange.title: React 19 is the current major

repos.why: A popular React component library that builds and tests against React 16.13 with enzyme-adapter-react-16; there is no enzyme adapter for React 19, so the test suite itself has to be migrated.

pendingChange.title: Node.js 16 is past end of life

source.quote: We are moving the End-of-Life date of Node.js 16 by seven months to coincide with the end of support of OpenSSL 1.1.1 on September 11th, 2023.

repos.why: The UI bundle for Spring's Antora docs sites: Node 16 sits in .nvmrc, engines and three workflows, and a leftover GitLab job still uses node:10, so every declaration has to move together around a gulp build.

pendingChange.title: Node.js 18 is past end of life

source.quote: Node.js 18 and all earlier versions are End-Of-Life.

repos.why: A small pnpm workspace app (VS Code for the web over Ethereum contracts) pinning Node 18 in two .nvmrc files, two engines fields and both workflows, with @types/node still on 16.

pendingChange.title: Nuxt 2 is past end of life

source.quote: Nuxt 2 will reach End of Life (EOL) on June 30th, 2024.

repos.why: Swell's official Nuxt 2 storefront theme (Vue 2, Vuex, @nuxtjs modules, engines Node 16.20); the hardest kind of framework-major move, with only a small jest suite and no CI to lean on.

pendingChange.title: Python 3.8 is past end of life

source.quote: As of 2024-10-07, 3.8 has reached the end-of-life phase of its release cycle.

repos.why: SAS's Viya 4 admin toolkit runs and tests only on Python 3.8 in CI with no declared floor; the upgrade moves the CI runtime and has to keep flake8 and 20 pytest modules passing on 3.12.

pendingChange.title: Flask 3 is the current major

repos.why: A purple-team operations app pinned to Flask 2.2.5 and Werkzeug 2.3 with a tangle of Flask extensions (Flask-Security and Flask-Security-Too, flask-mongoengine); CI runs the pytest suite in its Docker image.

pendingChange.title: Python 3.9 is past end of life

source.quote: As of 2025-10-31, 3.9 has reached the end-of-life phase of its release cycle.

repos.why: An embedded-testing tool whose CI and mypy target Python 3.9 while setup.cfg and the selftest mypy config still say 3.6; the upgrade must raise all four together and keep the typed selftests green.

pendingChange.title: Express 5 is the current major

source.quote: The focus of this release is on dropping old Node.js version support, addressing security concerns, and simplifying maintenance.

repos.why: A well-known Express 4 reference API (routes, middlewares, Mongo and Redis adapters) with no lockfile; Express 5 changes path matching and removed signatures. Its CI matrix also still runs Node 12 and 14.

pendingChange.title: Python 3.9 is past end of life

source.quote: As of 2025-10-31, 3.9 has reached the end-of-life phase of its release cycle.

tests.command: make test-ingester test-api && cd client && python -m pytest --import-mode=importlib ./datalake/tests/

repos.why: Planet's file-archive service (ingester, API, client) runs its API and ingester in a python:3.9 image (with a hard-coded python3.9 site-packages path) and tests the client on 3.8-3.12; the upgrade spans the Dockerfile, GitLab and GitHub CI and the client floor.

pendingChange.title: Node.js 18 is past end of life

source.quote: Node.js 18 and all earlier versions are End-Of-Life.

repos.why: A widely used streaming archive library whose engines floor is Node 18 and whose CI matrix and publish job test only EOL Node 18/20; a library-style upgrade of the floor and the test matrix.
